name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund spread near 160bp, above the 150bp Alert line; general strike on 5 Nov
state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was 159.9bp on 2 Nov, after peaking at 174.6bp on 22 Oct, and the OAT yield was just under 4.9% on 4 Nov (Journal du Coin; Trading Economics). The vote on the 2027 budget's revenue side has been postponed twice, with a deadline of 17 Nov, and unions strike on 5 Nov. No failed auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can feed into euro-area mortgage and business lending rates. Holders of French bonds or funds that own them are most exposed to price swings.

sources.title: Journal du Coin — Vie chère, spread à 160 points, mobilisation du 5 novembre

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
